Microchip Technology Announces PAC1761 And PAC1861 Families Of 65V Energy-Aware Digital Power Monitors
Microchip Technology announced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors that combine accumulated power-measurement insights with the necessary high-voltage measurement headroom and transient spike protection capabilities to help make 48V power architectures more efficient and resilient. The move to 48V power architectures demands that digital power monitors have an additional operational margin of up-to-65V measurement and 75V of spike protection to ensure transient survivability. The PAC1761 and PAC1861 devices add to these capabilities the intelligence to understand and react in real time to energy usage dynamics based on accumulated power measurement data.
Microchip?s digital power monitoring devices feature programmable alerts for voltage, current and power excursions, step-limit detection to identify sudden load changes, and configurable accumulated-energy thresholds that enable proactive system management based on both instantaneous and long-term power behavior. Target applications include automotive, AI/data center, networking, industrial, server, telecom/Power over Ethernet (PoE) and 48V power distribution systems. The 12-bit PAC1761 and 16-bit PAC1861 options are available in VDFN-8 (similar to SOT23-8), VDFN-10 and MSOP-10 packages including automotive-orderable variants. Pin-compatible options can reduce redesign risk, shorten qualification cycles and give customers flexibility to move between devices as requirements, availability, cost or performance change.
Development support includes evaluation board EV12R33A, a Python Command Line Interface (CLI) with library, Linux® driver and generic C library with multiple MCU code examples. Products in the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are available now starting at $0.56 each in 10,000-unit quantities for the PAC1761T-3E/E3 and PAC1861T-1E/3P, both in the MSOP-10 package. The price of the evaluation board EV12R33A is $49.00.

Navitas and Microchip Collaborate to Deliver 800V Reference Design for Next-Generation AI Data Centers
Solution combines digital power control, GaN technology, and hardware-based security to accelerate development of high-efficiency rack power systems based on the 800V DC OCP standard
TORRANCE, Calif. and CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) and Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) - As AI data centers scale to support high-power GPU clusters, the industry is shifting toward 800V DC rack power architectures to improve distribution efficiency, increase power density and support next-generation server designs. To help accelerate this transition, Navitas and Microchip have collaborated on an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for AI data center rack power applications.
The platform combines Microchip's digital power control and security technologies with Navitas' GaNFast™ gallium nitride (GaN) power devices to give developers a practical path to implement high-efficiency power conversion aligned with the Open Compute Project (OCP) 800V DC standard. Complete with reference hardware, software and design documentation, the solution helps reduce design risk, shorten development cycles and accelerate deployment of next-generation AI infrastructure.
"AI infrastructure optimization is driving one of the most significant power architecture transitions the data center industry has experienced in decades," said Joe Thomsen, corporate vice president of Microchip's digital signal controller business unit. "As the ecosystem moves toward higher-voltage rack power systems, developers need proven building blocks that help reduce design risk and accelerate innovation. Our collaboration with Navitas brings together complementary technologies to help customers navigate this transition and bring next-generation power solutions to market more quickly."
At the core of the reference platform are Microchip's dsPIC33AK Digital Signal Controllers (DSCs), TA100 CryptoAuthentication™ device, and Navitas' GaNFast FETs. The dsPIC33AK is designed to provide high-resolution control, high-speed analog and security with support for post-quantum cryptography. The devices offer library support for Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) Suite 2.0 recommended post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms and feature hardware accelerated cryptographic functions needed in Open Compute Project (OCP) power supplies and other connected real-time control designs. Powered by a 200 MHz 32-bit core with a double-precision floating-point unit (FPU), the dsPIC33AK256MPS306 family combines 78 ps high-resolution Pulse Width Modulators (PWMs) and multiple 12-bit Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) operating at up to 40 MSPS. The high-speed core and peripherals support fast, deterministic control loops for high frequency, high-efficiency DC/DC power conversion.
This PDB is powered by 16 × NV6034, 650 V, 17 mΩ GaNFast FETs in a stacked half-bridge topology on the primary side. The DFN8×8 dual-side-cooled package extends the performance advantages of GaN by reducing thermal resistance, allowing higher continuous power operation while maintaining exceptional efficiency. The PDB targets delivering up to 96% peak efficiency at full load with 1 MHz switching frequency, enabling a power density of 2,100 W/in³.
Approximately 20% thinner than a mobile phone, its ultra-low profile enables extremely close integration with the GPU board, maximizing transient performance and improving power distribution efficiency. Navitas' system-level approach ensures that advances in GaN technology translate into measurable improvements in efficiency, power density, transient performance, and total cost of ownership. Direct conversion from 800V DC to 6V DC combines both 800V DC to 50V DC and 50V DC to 6V DC conversion stages into one converter, delivering higher end-to-end efficiency.
"As AI infrastructure scales to support increasingly demanding computing platforms, Navitas' GaNFast technology is a critical enabler of higher power density, greater efficiency, and improved system performance," said Vipin Bothra, vice president of Global Solution Marketing at Navitas Semiconductor. "By combining Navitas' leadership in power semiconductors with Microchip's digital control expertise, this collaboration accelerates the delivery of advanced power solutions tailored to the evolving requirements of next-generation AI data centers."
The reference design also incorporates Microchip's TA100 CryptoAuthentication™ device to help address growing security requirements within modern power infrastructure. By integrating hardware-based security into the design, developers can establish a trusted foundation for system authentication and protection without the complexity of implementing security measures from scratch. The TA100 device provides support for code authentication (secure boot), Message Authentication Code (MAC) generation, trusted firmware updates, multiple key management protocols including Transport Layer Security (TLS) and other root-of-trust-based operations.
The Microchip and Navitas reference design provides a platform for developing high-voltage, high power, compact rack power systems for AI data centers. The design combines power control, security and GaN power technologies to support efficient 800V-to-6V-power conversion while helping system developers address evolving power delivery, performance and form-factor requirements. The solution will be showcased at Microchip's OCP Event, taking place October 12–15, 2026, in San Jose, California.
The design will be supported with a reference board, software and supporting documentation, giving developers access to the resources needed to evaluate and accelerate deployment of 800V DC power conversion systems for AI data center applications.
Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) is a next-generation power semiconductor leader in gallium nitride (GaN) and integrated-circuit devices, and high-voltage silicon carbide (SiC) technology. Navitas drives innovation across AI Infrastructure, combining Grid and Energy Infrastructure and AI data centers, as well as Performance Computing and Industrial Electrification. With more than 30 years of combined expertise in wide-bandgap technologies, GaNFast™ power ICs integrate GaN power, drive, control, sensing and protection to deliver faster power delivery, higher system density and greater efficiency. GeneSiC™ high-voltage SiC devices leverage patented Trench-Assisted Planar technology to provide industry-leading voltage capability, efficiency and reliability for medium-voltage grid and infrastructure applications. Navitas has more than 300 patents issued or pending and is the world's first semiconductor company to be CarbonNeutral® certified.

NVTS Stock In Spotlight Today Following Microchip Collaboration – Everything That Investors Need To Know
The companies combined Navitas’ power chips with Microchip’s control and security technology in a reference platform aimed at increasingly power-hungry AI server racks.
In this photo illustration, the logo of Navitas Semiconductor Corp is displayed on a smartphone screen, with the company's blue branding visible in the background. (Photo illustration by Cheng Xin/Getty Images)
The 20-kilowatt design converts an 800-volt rack supply directly to a fixed 6-volt server rail.
The platform targets up to 96% peak efficiency at full load.
Navitas has increasingly shifted its business toward AI infrastructure and other high-power markets.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Navitas Semiconductor Corp (NVTS) and Microchip Technology Inc. (MCHP) on Monday unveiled an 800-volt power reference design for next-generation artificial intelligence data centers as rising computing demand pushes server racks toward higher power levels.
The 20-kilowatt platform converts an 800-volt direct-current rack supply directly to a fixed 6-volt server rail, according to Microchip. In simpler terms, it reduces the voltage supplied inside the rack to a level usable closer to the computing hardware.
The design combines Navitas’ 650-volt gallium nitride, or GaN, power devices with Microchip’s digital-control and hardware-security technology. The companies said the platform targets up to 96% peak efficiency at full load.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
The system combines two conversion stages — from 800 volts to 50 volts and then from 50 volts to 6 volts — into a single converter, which the companies said improves end-to-end efficiency. Its low-profile design is also intended to allow closer integration with the graphics processing unit board.
As a reference design, the platform provides equipment makers with hardware, software, and documentation they can use to evaluate and develop their own 800-volt power systems rather than starting from scratch.
Navitas Pushes Deeper Into AI Infrastructure
The collaboration adds to Navitas’ shift away from mobile and consumer products toward higher-power markets.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
In fiscal second-quarter results, the company’s high-power revenue grew more than 50% year over year, and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, including data centers and grid infrastructure, was becoming a larger part of its business.
Navitas estimates that AI data centers, energy and grid infrastructure, performance computing, and industrial electrification together represent a $3.5 billion serviceable available market by 2030.
The company is also collaborating with Nvidia (NVDA) on an 800-volt high-voltage direct-current architecture designed to support 1-megawatt information-technology racks and beyond.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Microchip Expands Its AI Data Center Push
Microchip has also been expanding its exposure to AI data-center infrastructure. The company said its Data Center Solutions business generated $302.7 million in calendar 2025 revenue and expects that figure to grow about 65% to roughly $500 million in 2026.
What Retail Thinks About NVTS and MCHP Stocks
On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around NVTS stock remained in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory amid extremely high message volume. Meanwhile, sentiment around MCHP stock remained ‘bearish’.
So far this year, Navitas stock has rallied over 46%, while Microchip stock has risen nearly 25%. In comparison, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), which holds MCHP stock, has risen nearly 88% over the same period.

U.S. semiconductor company Microchip Technology’s Armenia operations and investment plans discussed in Yerevan - ARMENPRESS Armenian News Agency
U.S. semiconductor company Microchip Technology’s Armenia operations and investment plans discussed in Yerevan
Armenia’s Minister of High-Tech Industry and Artificial Intelligence Davit Tadevosyan received representatives of Microchip Technology, led by Shakeel Peera, Corporate Vice President of the corporation's FPGA business unit.
The Ministry said in a readout that the meeting focused on a number of issues related to the development and expansion of the company’s operations in Armenia.
The sides also discussed the company’s activities in Gyumri, Vanadzor and Ijevan, emphasizing the importance of Microchip Technology’s presence in developing the high-tech sector in the regions, attracting professional talent and strengthening local technology ecosystems.
The sides also discussed the approval of an export license obtained by the company in June 2026 from the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) for its operations in Armenia, as well as its potential impact on the company’s future activities, investment programs and development opportunities.
The meeting also addressed measures needed to ensure the necessary conditions for importing Microchip products into Armenia. In this context, the sides discussed ongoing talks between the Ministry and representatives of international semiconductor companies and the U.S. government on developing a categorized list of products.
The sides agreed to continue working to implement further steps in the areas discussed and expand cooperation.
Microchip Technology Inc. is an American semiconductor company that develops and manufactures microprocessors, FPGAs, analog and power-management solutions, as well as communications, memory and other embedded-system components. The company’s technologies are used in industry, automotive, aerospace and defense systems, communications, computing and other sectors.

MCHP Expands Ethernet Portfolio: Can it Challenge TXN & ADI?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:20 AM PDT 4 min read
Microchip Technology MCHP has expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with the launch of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 PMD transceivers and the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family with integrated transceivers. The products are designed for next-generation zonal architectures across automotive, industrial, robotics and aerospace and defense applications, extending Ethernet connectivity to edge nodes while reducing wiring and system complexity. The portfolio combines transceivers, endpoint functionality, power management and embedded-control capabilities, thereby supporting MCHP's broader Total System Solutions strategy. It also improves competitive prowess against the likes of Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI.
The LAN8679 features an Open Alliance 3-Pin interface in a compact package, while the LAN8680 adds power management, wake as well as sleep control and watchdog supervision. The LAN8660X/1X/2X family integrates a transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol solution, eliminating the need for external PHY components in applications such as control systems, lighting and audio. Microchip's 10BASE-T1S multidrop architecture can connect eight or more nodes over a single bus, helping reduce wiring weight, costs and gateway requirements.
The portfolio expansion strengthens Microchip's connectivity and networking growth strategy. The company identifies connectivity/networking as one of its new strategic growth pillars, targeting opportunities across Industry 4.0, automotive and data-center applications. MCHP highlights Single Pair Ethernet as a roughly $4-billion served available market, spanning automotive, aerospace, robotics, industrial vehicles, building controls, industrial controls, sensors, actuators and vehicle networking. The company also sees billions of legacy nodes as potential replacement opportunities, giving the expanded portfolio a sizable long-term addressable market.
The launch is also well timed with improving demand in MCHP's two largest target markets for these products. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, industrial represented 32.2% of revenues and automotive accounted for 15%. Industrial revenues increased 24.3% year over year, while automotive revenues jumped 29.3%. Industrial and automotive customers had largely completed inventory corrections, and Microchip noted that clients were placing a higher number of orders, while bookings remained strong across product lines, business units and geographies. The new devices are expected to help Microchip capture more semiconductor content as automotive and industrial networks migrate from fragmented legacy architectures toward consolidated Ethernet-based systems.
Texas Instruments' DP83TD555 targets 10BASE-T1S connectivity, while ADI's AD3300/AD3301 family brings integrated Ethernet connectivity to edge sensors and actuators.
Texas Instruments is challenging Microchip across automotive and industrial connectivity through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolio, strong manufacturing capacity and growing semiconductor content per system. In the second quarter of 2026, TXN's industrial revenues increased roughly 30% year over year, while automotive revenues rose in the mid-teens. Texas Instruments' supply capabilities further intensify the challenge. The company has available clean-room space and is expanding production capacity to address rising demand.
Analog Devices poses a significant challenge through its high-performance analog, sensing, power and embedded technologies. Industrial accounted for 49% of ADI's third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues and increased 53% year over year, led partly by automation, while automotive represented 25% of revenues and grew 16%. ADI said its higher content and share positions are driving automotive growth across next-generation ADAS, infotainment and electric powertrains. ADI is also positioning for the emergence of physical AI, including robotics and autonomous mobility.
MCHP's Share Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Shares of Microchip have appreciated 22% year to date, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's rise of 21.8%.
The MCHP stock is trading at a premium, with a trailing price/book multiple of 6.55 compared with the Zacks Semiconductor – Analog and Mixed industry's 6.48. Microchip has a Value Score of D.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Microchip's fiscal 2027 earnings is currently pegged at $3.63 per share, up 15.6% over the past 30 days, suggesting 121.3% growth from fiscal 2026's reported figure.

Microchip Technology stock (ISIN US5950171042) is trading firmer as of early September 2026 after the company reported new figures for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 and updated its outlook for the remainder of the year, according to a recent Form 8-K filing dated September 6, 2026.StockTitan SEC filings overview For investors, the key questions now center on how revenue growth, margins and cash generation can support the valuation in a volatile semiconductor cycle.
Fresh Q3 FY 2026 figures underpin the move
According to the furnished earnings release for Q3 fiscal 2026 attached to the Form 8-K, Microchip Technology reported revenue for the quarter in the low single-digit growth range versus the prior year, while maintaining an operating margin profile that remains well above many smaller peers.StockTitan SEC filings overview The reporting period covers the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, which ends within the last nine months relative to the September 7, 2026 publication date, and therefore represents the most current full set of figures from the company.
The same Q3 FY 2026 release highlights that Microchip Technology continued to generate solid earnings per share and free cash flow, with EPS and cash generation comfortably covering the quarterly dividend and leaving room for debt reduction and selective investment.StockTitan SEC filings overview For comparison, management notes that results reflect a more balanced demand environment than in earlier phases of the cycle, with industrial and automotive orders offsetting softer trends in some consumer-exposed segments, which suggests a more diversified earnings base than in prior years.
Guidance and risks in a choppy chip cycle
In its Q3 FY 2026 earnings release, Microchip Technology also provided guidance for the upcoming quarter within fiscal 2026, outlining expectations for revenue and margin trends under different demand scenarios.StockTitan SEC filings overview The company signaled that, while it anticipates continued support from long-cycle industrial and automotive programs, it remains cautious about the potential impact of broader macro uncertainty and inventory normalization across parts of the semiconductor supply chain.
For investors, one of the main risks is that a renewed slowdown in global manufacturing or a sharp adjustment in customer inventories could pressure order intake and utilization, which in turn would weigh on margins even if headline revenue holds up.StockTitan SEC filings overview Another factor to watch is competition in key microcontroller and analog markets, where pricing discipline and product differentiation are essential to defend share and profitability during periods of heightened capacity and aggressive bids by rivals.
Representative product: PIC microcontrollers
A central pillar of Microchip Technology's business model is its broad family of PIC microcontrollers, which serve as flexible computing building blocks in thousands of industrial, automotive and consumer applications worldwide. These microcontrollers are designed to offer a combination of low power consumption, robust peripheral integration and long product lifecycles, allowing customers to standardize on platforms and reduce redesign risk.

Microchip Expands Single Pair Ethernet Portfolio with New 10BASE‑T1S Devices Enabling Scalable Edge Connectivity
Microchip Technology Inc.
Microchip Technology Inc.
New transceivers and integrated endpoint family simplify zonal architectures and reduce system complexity for automotive and industrial applications
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the expansion of its 10BASE-T1S portfolio with the introduction of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 10BASE‑T1S PMD transceivers, alongside the LAN8660X/1X/2X family of endpoints with integrated transceivers. Designed to support next-generation zonal architectures, these solutions deliver flexible, space-efficient connectivity that extends Ethernet to the network edge.
As automotive, industrial and robotics systems evolve toward fully Ethernet-based networks, designers face increasing demands for simplified architectures, reduced wiring complexity and efficient edge node integration. Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S devices address these challenges and are designed to meet AEC-Q100 and ISO 26262 functional safety standards, building on Microchip's VelocityDRIVE™ portfolio with additional multidrop connectivity solutions featuring a standardized, streamlined interface.
The LAN8679 transceiver provides a standardized Open Alliance 3‑Pin (OA3P) interface in a compact 8‑pin VDFN package, supporting space-constrained edge nodes, while reducing pin count and design complexity. The LAN8680 builds on these capabilities by integrating System Basis Chip (SBC) features, including power management, system wake/sleep control and watchdog supervision. Both devices are engineered to enhance reliability and safety for demanding environments such as automotive and industrial applications.
"Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S portfolio advances our commitment to enabling scalable, all‑Ethernet network architectures," said Charlie Forni, corporate vice president of Microchip's networking and connectivity business unit. "By combining OA3P interface simplicity with integrated endpoint functionality, these devices give designers the flexibility to build efficient, reliable systems while significantly reducing complexity at the edge."
Complementing these devices, the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family integrates a PMD transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol (RCP) solution. This approach enables designers to deploy compact, fully integrated edge nodes for applications such as control systems, lighting and audio without the need for external PHY components.
By leveraging 10BASE‑T1S multidrop topology, Microchip's solutions allow multiple nodes—typically eight or more—to share a single bus line. This reduces wiring weight, lowers system costs and eliminates the need for gateways, making it easier to connect sensors and actuators directly to the network edge.
Microchip's expanded Single Pair Ethernet portfolio targets a wide range of applications, including automotive zonal architecture, industrial automation, robotics and aerospace and defense systems. The products align with industry trends toward consolidated networks and simplified connectivity frameworks, enabling designers to implement efficient and scalable all-Ethernet architectures. For more information about Microchip's Single Pair Ethernet solutions, visit the website.
The LAN8679, LAN8680 and LAN8660X/1X/2X are available in limited sampling. To learn more, please contact a Microchip sales representative.

This broad portfolio supports MCHP's Total System Solution strategy across microcontrollers, microprocessors, analog, FPGA, memory and connectivity products, while helping it compete with Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI in power management applications. MCHP also identifies AI/ML, data centers, edge computing, networking and connectivity as key growth areas.
Building on this foundation, Microchip Technology introduced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors for 48V architectures. The devices measure voltage, current, power and accumulated energy while offering transient protection, helping improve power efficiency, system reliability and energy visibility. The launch broadens MCHP's exposure to applications such as AI servers, networking equipment, automotive systems and industrial infrastructure. The company already targets power supplies, smart meters and energy monitoring, storage and server systems, and scale-up and scale-across AI infrastructure.
The expansion is particularly relevant to MCHP's growing data-center business. Data centers represented 17.1% of first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues, while data-center sales surged 97.8% year over year. Management said its data-center exposure spans power-management analog products, mixed-signal products, microcontrollers, security products, FPGAs, timing, memory, PCIe switches and storage controllers. MCHP revenues from catalog products sold into data centers are expected to increase from about $288 million in calendar 2025 to roughly $500 million in 2026. Including the Data Center Solutions business, MCHP expects total data-center revenues of about $1 billion in 2026, up roughly 69% year over year.
Management expects design wins across power management, mixed-signal, storage, security and connectivity products to support further data-center growth in 2027 and beyond. MCHP's catalog products are often designed into systems through power-supply manufacturers, module makers and card suppliers, giving the company indirect exposure to hyperscaler infrastructure deployments.
Texas Instruments is intensifying competition with MCHP through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolios. TXN highlighted that data-center revenues doubled year over year in the second quarter of 2026. Management also highlighted the transition toward 800V architectures, where power could move through stages such as 800V-to-48V and 48V-to-12V. This creates more conversion points and expands opportunities for TXN's analog, embedded-control and signal-chain products.
Analog Devices is challenging MCHP through a broader grid-to-chip power strategy spanning energy infrastructure, rack power and processor-level delivery. ADI said customers are using its solutions to achieve more than 98% conversion efficiency, multi-kilowatt power delivery, protection, telemetry and fault recording. Its 800V-to-intermediate conversion technologies can deliver 20 kilowatts at power densities above 2.5 kilowatts per cubic inch. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI also said data-center power revenues grew more than 100% year over year, while its Empower acquisition extends power delivery into the processor package, intensifying competition as AI infrastructure shifts toward higher-voltage, higher-density power architectures.

Solution combines digital power control, GaN technology, and hardware-based security to accelerate development of high-efficiency rack power systems based on the 800V DC OCP standard
TORRANCE, Calif. and CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) and Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) - As AI data centers scale to support high-power GPU clusters, the industry is shifting toward 800V DC rack power architectures to improve distribution efficiency, increase power density and support next-generation server designs. To help accelerate this transition, Navitas and Microchip have collaborated on an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for AI data center rack power applications.
The platform combines Microchip's digital power control and security technologies with Navitas' GaNFast™ gallium nitride (GaN) power devices to give developers a practical path to implement high-efficiency power conversion aligned with the Open Compute Project (OCP) 800V DC standard. Complete with reference hardware, software and design documentation, the solution helps reduce design risk, shorten development cycles and accelerate deployment of next-generation AI infrastructure.
"AI infrastructure optimization is driving one of the most significant power architecture transitions the data center industry has experienced in decades," said Joe Thomsen, corporate vice president of Microchip's digital signal controller business unit. "As the ecosystem moves toward higher-voltage rack power systems, developers need proven building blocks that help reduce design risk and accelerate innovation. Our collaboration with Navitas brings together complementary technologies to help customers navigate this transition and bring next-generation power solutions to market more quickly."
At the core of the reference platform are Microchip's dsPIC33AK Digital Signal Controllers (DSCs), TA100 CryptoAuthentication™ device, and Navitas' GaNFast FETs. The dsPIC33AK is designed to provide high-resolution control, high-speed analog and security with support for post-quantum cryptography. The devices offer library support for Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) Suite 2.0 recommended post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms and feature hardware accelerated cryptographic functions needed in Open Compute Project (OCP) power supplies and other connected real-time control designs. Powered by a 200 MHz 32-bit core with a double-precision floating-point unit (FPU), the dsPIC33AK256MPS306 family combines 78 ps high-resolution Pulse Width Modulators (PWMs) and multiple 12-bit Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) operating at up to 40 MSPS. The high-speed core and peripherals support fast, deterministic control loops for high frequency, high-efficiency DC/DC power conversion.
This PDB is powered by 16 × NV6034, 650 V, 17 mΩ GaNFast FETs in a stacked half-bridge topology on the primary side. The DFN8×8 dual-side-cooled package extends the performance advantages of GaN by reducing thermal resistance, allowing higher continuous power operation while maintaining exceptional efficiency. The PDB targets delivering up to 96% peak efficiency at full load with 1 MHz switching frequency, enabling a power density of 2,100 W/in³.
Approximately 20% thinner than a mobile phone, its ultra-low profile enables extremely close integration with the GPU board, maximizing transient performance and improving power distribution efficiency. Navitas' system-level approach ensures that advances in GaN technology translate into measurable improvements in efficiency, power density, transient performance, and total cost of ownership. Direct conversion from 800V DC to 6V DC combines both 800V DC to 50V DC and 50V DC to 6V DC conversion stages into one converter, delivering higher end-to-end efficiency.
"As AI infrastructure scales to support increasingly demanding computing platforms, Navitas' GaNFast technology is a critical enabler of higher power density, greater efficiency, and improved system performance," said Vipin Bothra, vice president of Global Solution Marketing at Navitas Semiconductor. "By combining Navitas' leadership in power semiconductors with Microchip's digital control expertise, this collaboration accelerates the delivery of advanced power solutions tailored to the evolving requirements of next-generation AI data centers."
The reference design also incorporates Microchip's TA100 CryptoAuthentication™ device to help address growing security requirements within modern power infrastructure. By integrating hardware-based security into the design, developers can establish a trusted foundation for system authentication and protection without the complexity of implementing security measures from scratch. The TA100 device provides support for code authentication (secure boot), Message Authentication Code (MAC) generation, trusted firmware updates, multiple key management protocols including Transport Layer Security (TLS) and other root-of-trust-based operations.
The Microchip and Navitas reference design provides a platform for developing high-voltage, high power, compact rack power systems for AI data centers. The design combines power control, security and GaN power technologies to support efficient 800V-to-6V-power conversion while helping system developers address evolving power delivery, performance and form-factor requirements. The solution will be showcased at Microchip's OCP Event, taking place October 12–15, 2026, in San Jose, California.
The design will be supported with a reference board, software and supporting documentation, giving developers access to the resources needed to evaluate and accelerate deployment of 800V DC power conversion systems for AI data center applications.

MCHP Expands Ethernet Portfolio: Can it Challenge TXN & ADI?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:20 AM PDT 4 min read
Microchip Technology MCHP has expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with the launch of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 PMD transceivers and the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family with integrated transceivers. The products are designed for next-generation zonal architectures across automotive, industrial, robotics and aerospace and defense applications, extending Ethernet connectivity to edge nodes while reducing wiring and system complexity. The portfolio combines transceivers, endpoint functionality, power management and embedded-control capabilities, thereby supporting MCHP's broader Total System Solutions strategy. It also improves competitive prowess against the likes of Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI.
The LAN8679 features an Open Alliance 3-Pin interface in a compact package, while the LAN8680 adds power management, wake as well as sleep control and watchdog supervision. The LAN8660X/1X/2X family integrates a transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol solution, eliminating the need for external PHY components in applications such as control systems, lighting and audio. Microchip's 10BASE-T1S multidrop architecture can connect eight or more nodes over a single bus, helping reduce wiring weight, costs and gateway requirements.
The portfolio expansion strengthens Microchip's connectivity and networking growth strategy. The company identifies connectivity/networking as one of its new strategic growth pillars, targeting opportunities across Industry 4.0, automotive and data-center applications. MCHP highlights Single Pair Ethernet as a roughly $4-billion served available market, spanning automotive, aerospace, robotics, industrial vehicles, building controls, industrial controls, sensors, actuators and vehicle networking. The company also sees billions of legacy nodes as potential replacement opportunities, giving the expanded portfolio a sizable long-term addressable market.
The launch is also well timed with improving demand in MCHP's two largest target markets for these products. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, industrial represented 32.2% of revenues and automotive accounted for 15%. Industrial revenues increased 24.3% year over year, while automotive revenues jumped 29.3%. Industrial and automotive customers had largely completed inventory corrections, and Microchip noted that clients were placing a higher number of orders, while bookings remained strong across product lines, business units and geographies. The new devices are expected to help Microchip capture more semiconductor content as automotive and industrial networks migrate from fragmented legacy architectures toward consolidated Ethernet-based systems.
Texas Instruments' DP83TD555 targets 10BASE-T1S connectivity, while ADI's AD3300/AD3301 family brings integrated Ethernet connectivity to edge sensors and actuators.
Texas Instruments is challenging Microchip across automotive and industrial connectivity through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolio, strong manufacturing capacity and growing semiconductor content per system. In the second quarter of 2026, TXN's industrial revenues increased roughly 30% year over year, while automotive revenues rose in the mid-teens. Texas Instruments' supply capabilities further intensify the challenge. The company has available clean-room space and is expanding production capacity to address rising demand.
Analog Devices poses a significant challenge through its high-performance analog, sensing, power and embedded technologies. Industrial accounted for 49% of ADI's third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues and increased 53% year over year, led partly by automation, while automotive represented 25% of revenues and grew 16%. ADI said its higher content and share positions are driving automotive growth across next-generation ADAS, infotainment and electric powertrains. ADI is also positioning for the emergence of physical AI, including robotics and autonomous mobility.

New transceivers and integrated endpoint family simplify zonal architectures and reduce system complexity for automotive and industrial applications
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the expansion of its 10BASE-T1S portfolio with the introduction of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 10BASE‑T1S PMD transceivers, alongside the LAN8660X/1X/2X family of endpoints with integrated transceivers. Designed to support next-generation zonal architectures, these solutions deliver flexible, space-efficient connectivity that extends Ethernet to the network edge.
As automotive, industrial and robotics systems evolve toward fully Ethernet-based networks, designers face increasing demands for simplified architectures, reduced wiring complexity and efficient edge node integration. Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S devices address these challenges and are designed to meet AEC-Q100 and ISO 26262 functional safety standards, building on Microchip's VelocityDRIVE™ portfolio with additional multidrop connectivity solutions featuring a standardized, streamlined interface.
The LAN8679 transceiver provides a standardized Open Alliance 3‑Pin (OA3P) interface in a compact 8‑pin VDFN package, supporting space-constrained edge nodes, while reducing pin count and design complexity. The LAN8680 builds on these capabilities by integrating System Basis Chip (SBC) features, including power management, system wake/sleep control and watchdog supervision. Both devices are engineered to enhance reliability and safety for demanding environments such as automotive and industrial applications.
"Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S portfolio advances our commitment to enabling scalable, all‑Ethernet network architectures," said Charlie Forni, corporate vice president of Microchip's networking and connectivity business unit. "By combining OA3P interface simplicity with integrated endpoint functionality, these devices give designers the flexibility to build efficient, reliable systems while significantly reducing complexity at the edge."
Complementing these devices, the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family integrates a PMD transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol (RCP) solution. This approach enables designers to deploy compact, fully integrated edge nodes for applications such as control systems, lighting and audio without the need for external PHY components.
By leveraging 10BASE‑T1S multidrop topology, Microchip's solutions allow multiple nodes—typically eight or more—to share a single bus line. This reduces wiring weight, lowers system costs and eliminates the need for gateways, making it easier to connect sensors and actuators directly to the network edge.
Microchip's expanded Single Pair Ethernet portfolio targets a wide range of applications, including automotive zonal architecture, industrial automation, robotics and aerospace and defense systems. The products align with industry trends toward consolidated networks and simplified connectivity frameworks, enabling designers to implement efficient and scalable all-Ethernet architectures. For more information about Microchip's Single Pair Ethernet solutions, visit the website.
The LAN8679, LAN8680 and LAN8660X/1X/2X are available in limited sampling. To learn more, please contact a Microchip sales representative.

Navitas and Microchip collaborated on an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for AI data center rack power applications, combining digital power control, GaN technology, and hardware-based security.
The reference design targets up to 96% peak efficiency at full load with 1 MHz switching frequency, enabling a power density of 2,100 W/in³.
Microchip's dsPIC33AK Digital Signal Controllers and Navitas' GaNFast FETs are key components of the reference platform.
The design incorporates Microchip's TA100 CryptoAuthentication device to address security requirements in power infrastructure.
The reference platform uses 16 × NV6034, 650 V, 17 mΩ GaNFast FETs in a stacked half-bridge topology.
The solution helps reduce design risk, shorten development cycles, and accelerate deployment of next-generation AI infrastructure.
